reviews.text: 评分：75 不错的类幸存者游戏，特点是装备系统和成就系统。 游戏寿命比想象中短，大约50小时左右，装备拿得差不多成就做得差不多也就索然无味了。 这类游戏的回味真是比较差，没什么记忆点而且游戏后期会越刷越疲劳。 优点是学习成本低，前中期正反馈足，比较适合快节奏生活的玩家。

As a lover of Vampire Survivors, I figured I'd like this and meant to pick it up at some point. Well, I finally did, and I adore it! It has the same addictive style, just with a Diablo coat of paint.. which as a lover of Diablo, that's pretty cool.

Survivor Type that looks like Diablo 1/2 Neat characters, a lot of items, quite a lot of ways to set up various builds. Huge meta-game progression: You have to do runs to retrieve equipment from the maps. Killing bosses gives you shards with which to further boost your characters. Torment mode also slowly unfolds by collecting Artifacts that modify and make the runs more difficult. If you want to see everything, you will grind *a lot*. But even if you don't care about grinding and just want to fire up a casual round the game holds up well. In my opinion, beats Vampire Survivors out of the park.

There is something about this game, which makes me love it, even though it's flaws continue to bug me. Sure, it's extremely unfriendly to beginners, and it takes a lot to get your feet moving, but once you figure it out, progress is so much more rewarding than easier/ simpler titles. *The slime enemies look like moving turds. No redeeming qualities there.
fantastic game, well done, reminds me of old diablo

A Dark-Fantasy Gem I can’t say enough good things about Halls of Torment. After more than 40 hours, I’m still having an absolute blast with it. This game simply oozes charm. It feels like a genuine love letter to classic PC gaming, game development, and dark fantasy. Art Style and Atmosphere The art style is fantastic, the atmosphere is wonderfully dark, and the music fits perfectly. Its environments and character models take me back to an older era of gaming, with a dark-fantasy feeling reminiscent of Warcraft II, but without the technical limitations or performance problems of that time. Even when the late-game Torments become incredibly chaotic and the screen fills with enemies and effects, the game continues to run beautifully. In more than 40 hours, it hasn’t failed me once. Classes and Gameplay Every class feels distinct, the builds are fun to experiment with, and there’s enough variety to keep each run feeling fresh. It’s the perfect “log in, do a run, and go about your day” kind of game—although, admittedly, I’ve been addicted to the gameplay loop ever since I bought it. Storytelling and Discovery I love the game’s light but atmospheric storytelling. It never overwhelms you with exposition, but there’s still enough voiced dialogue, environmental storytelling, and visual progression to make the world feel alive. Certain changes happen naturally as you play, eventually leading you toward completely new areas and bosses. The game trusts you to notice these things for yourself, which makes discovering them feel much more rewarding. After about 20 hours, I thought I had seen nearly everything the game had to offer. Then it continued surprising me. The Bard The biggest surprise came when I finally unlocked the Bard. Until that point, the classes had mostly followed recognizable fantasy archetypes. There’s absolutely nothing wrong with that—the game executes those archetypes extremely well—but it also created a certain expectation. When I selected the Bard, I honestly wasn’t expecting very much. Then I played him, and—oh my God—he was so freaking cool. Without spoiling anything, the Bard felt like the developers giving one enormous “thank you” to everyone who had stayed with the game long enough to unlock him. His presentation and gameplay were such an unexpected delight that it felt like the game was celebrating alongside me. It was one of those rare unlocks that genuinely made me stop and appreciate just how much creativity, passion, and care had gone into the experience. Final Thoughts At its current price, Halls of Torment is an absolute steal. It delivers satisfying progression, distinct classes, creative builds, excellent performance, atmospheric storytelling, and lovingly recreated old-school visuals. The ending also appears to tease some kind of continuation. Whether that means DLC, an expansion, or an entirely new game, I’ll be there for it. Halls of Torment is an absolute gem, and I’m incredibly glad I stumbled across it. I can’t recommend it enough. 10/10

玩了也有快30小时了，刚开始是看有点暗黑风就入了，刚玩几把，感觉也就那么回事，为什么差评，游戏有几个问题，首先是游戏正反馈几乎没有，局内成长非常低，升级就是最基本的属性提升，还很小，没有其他肉鸽游戏那种bulid成型就质变那种，就纯坐牢，被怪当狗溜，局外成长更是等于没有；第二，游戏的特色应该是类暗黑那种装备系统，然而纯粹就一噱头，装备非常少，还没什么词条；第三，不含DLC就5关，500个成就在那无限进去刷，一晚能睡着好几次。综上所述给了差评，图一新鲜，玩几把就卸载的，可以尝尝鲜，不收集齐就难受，有强迫症的，离这游戏远点。

煎熬，劝想要闲余时间玩的玩家还是不要入坑了。 游戏制作者相当喜欢在各种地方加入一点折磨玩家的小巧思，而且正反馈是极少的，内容是匮乏的。 打的时候全程被怪当狗溜，打不过，跑不过， 而且能提升的方式相当少，局内build更是幽默，我说白了，这款游戏比其他游戏更需要“超武”这种定位的东西来缓解后期压力，但制作者显然不这么想。 最后，如果你想深入游玩，你会发现这款游戏在各种细微之处都藏了史，怎么不爽怎么来，怎么恶心怎么来，说白了就是越玩越恶心。

中规中矩的幸存者游戏, 能玩但不怎么好玩. 复古画面有特色比起其它热门幸存者游戏称得上精致, 但贴图感还是很重; 怪物设计有特点, 每种怪物有自己的小机制, 不完全是朝着玩家跑千篇一律换贴图, 但玩起来都是小怪放风筝boss躲弹幕体验差别不明显; 地图有隐藏解谜, 但跑起来很烦, 距离特别长又要兼顾刷怪捡经验还没有小地图, 继承了所有幸存者游戏会有的缺点; 每局固定30分钟还是太漫长了, 对想要找个肉鸽能没事开一把消磨时间的人来说这个游戏并不是好的选择. 只推荐会喜欢吸血鬼幸存者而且想找个相似游戏的玩家尝试

As far as the game's fun factor goes, it's average—neither particularly good nor particularly bad. It's just that updates are hopelessly slow, and bug fixes are hopelessly slow too—those aspects are the worst. It's taking far too long, even though there are parts that need to be corrected. This game has little content and no potential; its future looks bleak. There is an extreme disparity between strong and weak abilities, resulting in very poor game balance. Half of the abilities are weak and underperform, so they're unusable.

I don't know what happened to this game. I used to really enjoy playing it, but lately the RNG has been making it a lot less fun. I used to challenge myself with Agony mode and different reroll setups, but now it feels like every map beyond the base game is way harder than it needs to be. Breaking barrels and only getting cheese over and over, especially in Agony mode, gets frustrating fast when weapon drops are nowhere to be found. I also have all these potions for rerolling traits, but half the time I just get options that my hero doesn't even need. It makes the whole reroll system feel pointless. On top of that, there are bugs that make the experience worse. I've had enemies burrow underground, disappear from view, and then suddenly damage me when they aren't even visible on screen. That's not challenging it's just annoying. The more I play, the more I find myself getting frustrated instead of having fun. Between bad rerolls, useless item drops, and enemies bugging out, it feels like every patch fixes one thing and introduces a new set of problems. I genuinely used to love this game, but lately it feels like it's gone from bad to worse. I really hope the bugs get fixed and that the RNG gets adjusted, especially for the higher difficulty modes. Also, getting a bucket after killing a tough boss feels like a slap in the face. I've had runs where I killed three bosses in a row and all of them dropped buckets. If buckets are supposed to be useful, then maybe increase the drop rate of items players don't already have, or add some way to target armor and other gear that's still missing from their collection. Right now, I mostly end up getting duplicates or items that don't make sense for the hero I'm playing, which just adds to the frustration.

Among dozens of surviorslikes I have played, Halls of Torment is quite mediocre. Around 10 hours in it gets quite boring and a slogfest. I like to play with autoattack on and the game does a poor job of telling me when the autoattack is on or off. Usually I notice it way too late. Among plethora of issues I have with it are also bad visual clarity of understanding where it is safe to move and where are the danger zones, which projectiles are mine and which are hostile. Especially dumb when some levels only use one color palette that matches some abilities so I can barely even see what is going on. Main currency in the game is Gold and it is so slow to gain and everything is Gold-gated. Getting XP gain bonuses from completing quests is cool, but that also slows down and eventually turns into gameplay of hunting specific quests to progress instead of just playing and progressing naturally. I even had the Boglands DLC (region which I did get Unlocked and the Lord defeated and Agony mode done), but it just gets too boring. It is cool that there are many characters, but a lot of them are really bad if you dont have the item sets yet. So playing variety early is equivalent to shooting myself in the foot over and over. Got tired of doing that. Game lacks active mobility features like dashing or dodging. It is overall quite basic. Does not seem like there is any co-op or multiplayer either (I personally do not care about that). The game has clearly potentially hundreds of hours worth of unlocks, but the core gameplay is too slow to ever get to that point. Also I noticed myself checking the game timer very often and finding that the time passed is so much less than expected. A good game makes me not notice time passing fast and Halls of Torment just does not do it for me. Would rather recommend checking out Death Must Die, Soulstone Survivors or Brotato for better games like this.

是日，恶魔大军于村外集结，战士、弓手、术士、法师一众将领等被困村中，需得在恶魔围攻中生存两刻时间，方可引出恶魔主将，将其诛杀。 当晚，众将集结共商退敌之策，法师首先说道：“各位英雄，依我之见，退敌唯有一策。” 众将闻言，抬头看向法师，待他续述退敌之法，却见法师摇了摇头，欲言又止。 战士上前一步，将手放在法师肩头，说道：“汝有退敌之策，为何不说？” 法师道：“此策与我法术相合，却怕与你们不合，害你们送了性命。” 术士笑道：“多虑了！想必各位心中也有退敌之策。”说罢，术士环顾四周，见众人纷纷点头，便继续说道：“不如我们将自己的退敌之策写在掌心，一齐展示。” 众人附议，纷纷转身在手上写下退敌之策。术士见众人已写好，便说道：“请大家举起手掌，然后看看别人写了什么。” 众人举起手掌，同时看向他人的手掌。一时间，众人开怀大笑，笑声在天地间回荡。 原来，所有人都不约而同地在手掌上写下了两个单词：“Dragon’s Breath”。
